name: MonarchSearchResultItem
title: SearchResultItem
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.ListItem with an AnnotatedString title and snippet, androidx.compose.foundation.clickable
summary: One search result: a title, a breadcrumb path, a snippet with the matched words highlighted, a leading file icon or tile and trailing meta.
whenToUse: In the results of an in-app search, a command palette or a help search, one row per result. Pass the words typed with monarchQueryTerms, or the match ranges or <mark> markers the search service returns.
whenNotToUse: For a plain list row without a query use the Material 3 ListItem. For a suggestion under a search field use the suggestions of MonarchSearchBar.
api: @Composable public fun MonarchSearchResultItem(title: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, path: List<String> = emptyList(), snippet: String? = null, terms: List<String> = emptyList(), titleRanges: List<TextRange>? = null, snippetRanges: List<TextRange>? = null, snippetMarkTags: Boolean = false, fileName: String? = null, enabled: Boolean = true, onClick: (() -> Unit)? = null, icon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, meta: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, pathLabel: String? = null, interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null)

options.name: title
options.description: The result's title, as plain text.

options.name: path
options.description: Breadcrumb segments, shown with a slash between them and spoken as Location followed by the segments.

options.name: snippet
options.description: A short excerpt of the matching content, as plain text, at most three lines.

options.name: terms
options.description: Words to highlight in the title and snippet, matched without regard to case, longest first. Use monarchQueryTerms.

options.name: titleRanges
options.description: Exact matches in the title as UTF-16 offsets with an exclusive end, the numbers the web and most search services use. Replaces terms for the title. Overlapping ranges are merged; ranges past the end are clamped.

options.name: snippetRanges
options.description: Exact matches in the snippet. Replaces terms for the snippet.

options.name: snippetMarkTags
options.description: The snippet carries <mark> and </mark> markers, for example from PostgreSQL ts_headline. Only those two markers are read; other markup stays text.

options.name: fileName
options.description: A file name; its MonarchFileTypeIcon fills the leading slot. Takes precedence over icon.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether the row responds. A disabled row draws its text in the disabled color.

options.name: onClick
options.description: Called when the row is activated. With it the row is one button and the title takes the link color.

options.name: icon
options.description: A leading icon or avatar on a muted tile. Decorative.

options.name: meta
options.description: Trailing details such as a badge, a date or an owner, in the caption type and the muted color.

options.name: pathLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in Location spoken before the path.

options.name: interactionSource
options.description: The source of the press, focus and hover interactions of the row.

states.name: interactive
states.description: With onClick: the title is in the link color, the row shows the ripple when pressed and the focus ring when focused.

states.name: plain
states.description: Without onClick: the title is in the default text color and the row is static text.

states.name: disabled
states.description: The title, path, snippet and meta use the disabled text color and the row does not respond.

appearance: The title is in the label type, in the link color (or the default text color); the path is a caption in the muted text color with the slashes in the subtle text color; the snippet is muted body text. Matched words have the subtle warning fill, the default text color and a semibold weight. The leading tile is the muted background with a muted icon. The row has no fill of its own.
platformNotes: The web renders the title as a link (href) or a button, accepts a router link component and a roving tab index. On Android the row runs onClick, and the app navigates from there; roving focus is the list's own keyboard focus. The web's queryTerms is monarchQueryTerms, and ranges are TextRange (start inclusive, end exclusive, UTF-16, as the web). iOS names the action parameter action and the leading SF Symbol systemImage; Android uses onClick and an icon slot, because Monarch bundles no icons. The web moves the meta under the text on narrow screens; the Material ListItem keeps it at the end. The match fill has no padding or rounded corner, which a span background cannot draw.
accessibility: The row is one TalkBack element that reads the title, then Location and the path segments separated by commas, then the snippet, then the meta.
With onClick the row has the button role and one activation; without it the row has no click action.
Matches are also semibold, so they do not depend on the fill color; the highlight itself is not read.
The leading icon or file icon is decorative.
An interactive row has a 48dp touch target; the title wraps whole at font scale 2.0.
edgeCases: Terms that are empty or only spaces highlight nothing.
Terms are matched as text, not as patterns: a dot in a term matches only a dot.
Ranges that overlap are merged and ranges past the end of the text are clamped; an empty range is ignored.
Any markup other than <mark> and </mark> in the snippet is shown as text.
A snippet longer than three lines ends with an ellipsis; the title is never shortened.

examples.title: Link result with path and highlighted snippet
examples.webExample: Link result with path and highlighted snippet
examples.template:
MonarchSearchResultItem(
    title = {{title}},
    path = listOf({{path.0}}, {{path.1}}),
    snippet = {{snippet}},
    terms = monarchQueryTerms({{query}}),
    onClick = {},
    icon = { MonarchIcon(SampleIcons.Inbox, contentDescription = null) },
    meta = { MonarchBadge(text = {{badge}}) },
)
examples.code:
MonarchSearchResultItem(
    title = "Travel policy",
    path = listOf("Handbook", "Policies"),
    snippet = "Book travel at least two weeks ahead and add the trip to the shared calendar.",
    terms = monarchQueryTerms("travel calendar"),
    onClick = {},
    icon = { MonarchIcon(SampleIcons.Inbox, contentDescription = null) },
    meta = { MonarchBadge(text = "Document") },
)

examples.title: A file with ranges and marks from the search service
examples.code:
MonarchSearchResultItem(
    title = "Q3 travel budget.xlsx",
    titleRanges = listOf(TextRange(3, 9)),
    snippet = "Flights and <mark>hotels</mark> by team.",
    snippetMarkTags = true,
    fileName = "Q3 travel budget.xlsx",
    onClick = {},
)
